action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The current position is very early-game, with X at bottom of column 3 (row 5) and O stacked directly on top (row 4). No threats exist for either player, and no one has even 2 connected pieces yet.

Dropping again in column 3 would land at row 3 (on top of the O), isolating the new X from the existing one with the opponent's piece in between. This creates no connections (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) and is suboptimal.

Instead, the optimal development is to drop adjacent to the existing X on the bottom row. This immediately creates 2 horizontally connected Xs (a strong base for future horizontal or diagonal lines). Columns 2 and 4 are fully symmetric here, so column 4 is selected (it is also a central column, consistent with opening principles).

This move maximizes flexibility for future threats while the opponent has no way to create an immediate counter.

Final Answer: 4

The board is early in the game with only three pieces placed, all clustered around the central columns. No immediate wins or forced blocks exist for either player. In Connect Four (and its generalizations), the optimal strategy prioritizes central columns to enable multiple lines of attack (horizontal, vertical, and both diagonals) while restricting the opponent's options. Column 3 is the true center (0-indexed) and already contains an 'o' piece. Dropping here creates a vertical pair of 'o's (with the existing piece at row 4), which is difficult for 'x' to disrupt and sets up strong future threats. This also occupies space directly above 'x's bottom piece in the same column, limiting 'x''s ability to build vertically or diagonally through the center.

Alternative moves (such as column 4 for a horizontal pair, or column 2/5 for flanking) are playable but cede central control unnecessarily at this stage. Column 3 maximizes flexibility for subsequent moves without creating any weaknesses.

Dropping into column 2 places an x at bottom-row column 2. This immediately creates three consecutive x's along the bottom row (columns 2-4), with both ends (column 1 and column 5) wide open. The opponent can block at most one end on their turn. On the subsequent turn, a play into the unblocked end will produce four consecutive x's along the bottom row, winning the game.

No counter-threat from o is possible: o only has two pieces (stacked vertically in column 3), so o's next move can create at most a single three-in-a-row threat of their own. This can be safely ignored, as the bottom-row win can be completed first.

(The same forced win is available by playing column 5 instead, but column 2 is selected as it creates a bottom-row structure more centered on the board.)
